items.title: ‘Spotify is now an agent’ – Co-CEO outlines company’s AI plan
items.excerpt: Following the launches of personal agents such as Meta's Muse, OpenAI's Dots and Anthropic's Claude Duet, Spotify's co-CEO laid out how the service plans to become the music layer AI agents call on.

items.title: Spotify Co-CEOs Talk AI Remixing Tool: ‘We’re the Right Company to Do This’
items.excerpt: On Spotify's Q3 call, its co-CEOs discussed the coming AI remixing and covers tool for subscribers, pitching it as a licensed creation feature that will generate new revenue for rightsholders.

items.title: Stop sending me vibecoded plugins, I’m begging you
items.excerpt: MusicTech's inbox is drowning in AI-vibecoded audio plugins; the piece explains why that is a problem for producers and highlights indie developers who are using AI-assisted development responsibly.

items.title: 멜론 3위 오른 AI 노래, 어떻게 만들었나…‘머무르’ 제작팀 인터뷰
items.excerpt: The team behind the AI-made song '꿈꾸던 어른이 되었나요?', which reached No.3 on Melon and No.2 on YouTube Music, explains its production workflow and how human writing and AI generation were combined.

items.title: Is There a Future for 'Humanoid Robot Performances'? South Korea’s Galaxy Corporation Thinks So
items.excerpt: South Korea-based Galaxy Corporation is combining entertainment IP, AI and humanoid robots for an upcoming Halloween-themed performance event in California.

items.title: ICMP Tells Australian Legislators Major Hits Were Already Used to Train AI Without Compensation
items.excerpt: Publisher body ICMP warns that Australian copyright law risks being watered down for AI training, citing songs by Kylie Minogue and Nick Cave already used to train models without payment.

items.title: Controllable Mono-to-Stereo Upmixing using Reward-tilted Flows
items.excerpt: A flow-matching upmixer that generates realistic stereo from single-channel recordings, with reward tilting to give engineers control over the resulting stereo image.

items.title: AI-Generated Music and the Future of Creativity Discussed at Billboard Latin Music Week
items.excerpt: A Billboard Latin Music Week panel with Cristina Perpiñá-Robert and Pierre Hachar Jr. debated how AI is used in Latin music creation and how to protect human creators.

items.title: AI가 만든 음악, 기술로 가려낸다 … 디텍트엑스, 정부 출연 연구기관 기술성 평가 성적 확보
items.excerpt: Korean startup DetectX's AI-generated-music verification solution passed a technical evaluation by a government research institute, positioning it for copyright management of AI tracks.

items.title: Fender Studio Pro 8.2 Update: New Mixing and Workflow Features
items.excerpt: Studio Pro 8.2 expands its built-in stem separation to isolate guitar and piano for conversion to MIDI, adds a sub-3ms low-latency Vocal Tune mode, trim automation and multiple marker tracks.

items.title: Is The Humanity of Instruments Under Threat from AI?
items.excerpt: Amid a surge of vibe-coded instrument plugins, gearnews asks whether AI-built instruments risk losing the human design choices that make instruments expressive.

items.title: AI 음악 기술 '뉴튠', 오디오비주얼 에이전트 DJ '탈' ADE 2026서 첫 공개
items.excerpt: Korean AI music company Neutune unveiled 'Tal', an audiovisual AI agent DJ project backed by KOCCA's AI content programme, at Amsterdam Dance Event 2026.

items.title: [단독] 'AI 음악' 저작권 신청 1년새 500% 급증…기준 미비에 전부 '미등록'
items.excerpt: Copyright filings for AI-assisted songs at KOMCA rose from 133 to 759 in a year, but all 892 applications remain unregistered because there is no standard for judging human creative contribution.

items.title: AI Girl Group BABYQUEEN Draws Criticism After One of Its Members Gets 'Pregnant'
items.excerpt: An AI-generated Chinese girl group drew backlash on social media after a storyline had one of its virtual members announce a pregnancy, raising questions about synthetic-idol narratives.

items.title: FLOMSS: Generative Music Source Separation by Flow Matching
items.excerpt: A systematic study of flow matching as a generative approach to four-stem music source separation (vocals, bass, drums, other) on full-band audio, an alternative to the discriminative separators behind today's stem splitters.
